method: Whisper tiny.en re-transcription of final mixed MP4, compared with intended narration. ASR differences need interpretation; this is not proof of word-perfect audio.
transcript: Your data is already in Microsoft Fabric. What if you could ask it a question and inspect the query behind the answer? This is Microsoft's documented data agent example. A question goes in, an answer comes back with the steps used to retrieve it. Here is the workflow, create the agent, choose its data, then ask, inspect and test. In your Fabric workspace, select new item. Search for Fabric data agent, select it, and give your agent a name. Next, add your data source from the one-late catalog. That could be a lake house, a warehouse, or a power BI semantic model. In Explorer, choose the relevant tables. Watch the check boxes. You control which tables are available to the agent. Add instructions that define your business terms. Tell the agent which source to use for different kinds of questions. Now, ask a concrete question. Microsoft's example asks how many users played Contoso games, and how many users purchased items in those games? Here is the important part. Expand the steps and inspect the generated query. Check the filters, the tables, and the answer. A data agent can retrieve structured answers. A question about why sales changed needs more evidence. Retrieving a number does not prove its cause. Create, choose, verify. Start with one question you can check, then test more questions before you publish. That is a useful first fabric data agent.
